name: Quepos
catalog_citation: Quesada Pacheco, Miguel Ángel. 1996. El idioma de los quepos. Estudios de Lingüística Chibcha (Universidad de Costa Rica) 15: 59-76.
catalog_locator: p. 69, section 3.4 '¿Acento o tono en quepo?'
catalog_quote: Nada, o casi nada, se puede decir del acento -mucho menos del tono- en quepo, ya que, en primer lugar, no existe ninguna palabra en este idioma que haya sobrevivido; en segundo lugar, los materiales con que se cuenta para el presente estudio no permiten identificar posiciones acentuales, debido a la escasez de datos. En algunos casos se presentan alternancias vocálicas en posición final, lo cual da a entender que, al menos, la vocal final no llevaba el acento principal: Beara - Beare, Oco - Ocu. En estos casos, pareciera que el quepo tenía palabras graves.

new_statements.translation: Nothing, or almost nothing, can be said about accent - much less about tone - in Quepo, since, first, no word of this language has survived; second, the materials available for this study do not allow accentual positions to be identified, owing to the scarcity of data. In some cases vowel alternations appear in final position, which suggests that, at least, the final vowel did not carry the main accent: Beara ~ Beare, Oco ~ Ocu. In these cases it would seem that Quepo had paroxytone (penult-stressed) words.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File held by the project (18-pp image-only PDF, PDF 1.0, no text; A's scanned extract 1091 lines). scanned header reads 'Lingüística Chibcha 15:59-76, 1996 / EL IDIOMA DE LOS QUEPOS / Miguel Ángel Quesada Pacheco, Universidad de Bergen'. Section '3.4 ¿Acento o tono en quepo?' is at extract lines 577-589 under the running head 'QUESADA PACHECO: ELCh: El idioma de los quepos 69'; A's quote matches the scanned text word for word, and the following paragraph on Areba - Arebe - Aribe ('De serlo, sería un caso de palabra esdrújula, pues la única vocal que permanece invariable es la <a> en posición inicial') matches A's exceptions entry. Identity: intro and sec. 2 place the quepos on the Pirrís/Pa…
new_statements.relation_note: Sec. 3.1 tentative consonant inventory from graphemes (p, t, k, b, d, g, f(1x), s, x, h, ch, ng(1x), r/rr, l, y, w); 3.2 five-vowel system, <e> never initial, double-vowel spellings (Baaraga, Ooro) possibly long vowels or hiatus/glottal; 3.3 semiconsonants; 3.4 accent/tone undeterminable (quoted); 3.5 syllable types CV-dominant, no CC; 4-5 areal comparison: shares features with Huetar and Boruca but 'era un idioma independiente, que no era ni huetar ni boruca'; at most closely related to Boruca.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Author states accent position (and a fortiori tone) cannot be determined from the surviving material (16th-17th c. Spanish transcriptions of proper names); the only hint is that final-vowel spelling alternations (Beara~Beare, Oco~Ocu) suggest the final vowel was unstressed, i.e. possibly penultimate stress in those names; Areba~Arebe~Aribe, if one name, would be antepenultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: Areba - Arebe - Aribe: if the same anthroponym, 'sería un caso de palabra esdrújula' (antepenult), since only initial <a> is invariant; author flags no certainty it is one name.
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly about the language of the Quepos of the Pirrís/Parrita area (Pacific Costa Rica), cacique Corrohore, Vázquez de Coronado 1563; the only linguistic study of Quepo ever published. Material: the plant name chiro/chirob and 93 Quepo anthroponyms from a 1616 encomienda list (Archivo Nacional de Costa Rica, Mortual Cartago 917), analysed graphemically for a tentative sound inventory, vowels, syllable structure and areal comparison with Huetar [huet1234] and Boruca [boru1236]. Not in Glottolog's reference list for quep1238 (which is empty); live UCR URL now redirects to a login page, Internet Archive copy is open.

sources.note: Modern authoritative statement by the leading Chibchanist on which 16th-century Costa Rican languages (incl. Quepo) are attested and how they are affiliated (Quepo usually conjectured Boruca- or Huetar-related on onomastic grounds); would document 'unattested' status first-hand. No stress content expected.

sources.citation: Quesada Pacheco, Miguel Ángel. 2009. El panteón lingüístico chibcha y sus vecinos. Letras (Universidad Nacional, Heredia, Costa Rica) 45: 11-24.
sources.note: Nothing specific to Quepo. General: substrate words in descendant communities 'podrían.. dar pistas para el conocimiento de la prosodia de dichas lenguas, rasgo suprasegmental casi ausente en los materiales documentales escritos' (p. 23). For Boruca (another language) it mentions 'un sistema de tonos, uno alto y otro bajo'.

sources.citation: Quesada Pacheco, Miguel Ángel. 2006. Toponimia indígena de Costa Rica. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 32(2): 203-259.
sources.note: Nothing on accent or tone. Note 10: in contrast with Huetar, frequent initial <b, d>; in contrast with Boruca, apparently long vowels (double-vowel spellings <Baaraga>, <Ooro>), citing Quesada Pacheco 1996c: 68. States the Quepo idiom 'representaría un conjunto fónico autónomo' distinct from Huetar and Boruca; Quepos and Barú possibly of Quepo origin.
